name: PoWA
summary: PostgreSQL Workload Analyzer: snapshots pg_stat_statements and related extensions into a PostgreSQL repository, and shows per-query history, wait events and index suggestions in a web UI.
intro: PoWA is built from PostgreSQL extensions and two small programs. `pg_stat_statements` is the one required data source: it keeps cumulative counters per normalized query. Optional extensions add more: `pg_qualstats` samples the predicates in `WHERE` and `JOIN` clauses, `pg_stat_kcache` adds the real reads and writes the filesystem did for each query, `pg_wait_sampling` samples wait events and `pg_track_settings` records configuration changes and restarts. The `powa` extension, powa-archivist, takes snapshots of these counters on a schedule (every 5 minutes by default), stores them compactly and purges old data (after 1 day by default). powa-web, a Python and Tornado application, turns the deltas between snapshots into graphs per server, database and query.

There are two ways to run it. In local mode a background worker inside each server takes the snapshots, which needs a restart, adds overhead, and can’t work on read-only standbys. The recommended remote mode, added in PoWA 4 (2020), stores everything on a separate repository database: the powa-collector daemon connects to each registered server, including standbys, and copies the snapshots there. With `pg_qualstats` installed, PoWA suggests missing indexes for one query or the whole workload of a database, and with HypoPG on the target database it creates each suggested index hypothetically and checks with `EXPLAIN` whether the planner would use it. PoWA is free under the PostgreSQL License. Version 5.0 (November 2024) was a rework with no upgrade path; 5.3, in August 2026, followed changes in the PostgreSQL 19 betas.
strengths: History per normalized query: calls, time, rows, block I/O and, with `pg_stat_kcache`, real filesystem reads and writes, for every snapshot
Index suggestions for a whole database’s workload, checked with hypothetical indexes before you build anything
Remote mode keeps the stored data and the UI’s queries off production servers and covers standbys
Its extensions also cover `pg_stat_activity`, `pg_stat_io`, replication, WAL, archiver and wait events, so one UI shows server-wide activity too
limits: Each monitored server still needs `pg_stat_statements` and any other stats extensions in `shared_preload_libraries`, which means a restart and, on managed services, only the extensions the provider offers
Several parts to install and keep in step: extensions on every server, a repository database, powa-collector and powa-web; 5.0 had no upgrade path from 4.x
Reports rely on counters only ever growing; calling `pg_stat_statements_reset()` makes them meaningless for that period
`pg_qualstats` samples 1% of queries by default, so index suggestions need time or a higher sample rate, which costs performance on busy servers

story: PostgreSQL’s `pg_stat_statements` shows totals since the last reset, not how a query behaved yesterday at 3 p.m. PoWA began at the PostgreSQL company DALIBO in 2014 to keep snapshots of those counters and chart them; its first releases had a Perl web interface built on Mojolicious.

PoWA 2.0, in March 2015, split the project into powa-archivist, the extension that stores snapshots, and powa-web, a rewritten interface in Python on Tornado, and added `pg_qualstats` and `pg_stat_kcache`. PoWA 3.0, in December 2015, used predicate statistics to propose the smallest set of indexes for a whole database, checked with HypoPG’s hypothetical indexes. PoWA 4.0, in April 2020, added remote mode and powa-collector, so data could live on a separate server and standbys could be monitored.

Since 2018 the copyright has been held by the PoWA team rather than DALIBO. PoWA 5.0 followed in November 2024 as a rework that adds server-wide statistics views; releases in 2026 have kept pace with PostgreSQL 19.

choices.choice: Build on PostgreSQL extensions rather than an external agent
choices.why: The statistics already live inside the server, in `pg_stat_statements` and friends, so an extension can read them and keep a consistent view across PostgreSQL versions.
No extra database to run: the history is ordinary tables that PoWA aggregates and purges, and powa-web reads them with SQL.

choices.choice: Add a remote mode in version 4
choices.why: A background worker on each server cost performance, needed restarts and couldn’t write on read-only standbys; a collector writing to a separate repository fixed all three.
